content:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: p99 latency SLO breach detected for route `/v1/stream` on cluster `serve-prod` (since 1954321975). Metric: p99 = 3.8s (SLO 2.0s). Suspected GPU node degradation on node `gpu-node-7` (ECC warnings). Auto-escalation: paging on-call ML and infra.

ashley: I'm seeing the alert, looking at console now. tagging @sophia (oncall-ml) and @mike (oncall-infra) to take.

sophia: jumping in. can someone paste recent p99/p95 graphs? I see streaming tail spikes in the dashboard.

zack: here's quick snapshot from dashboards: p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 3.6-4s, error rate for streaming chunked responses up ~9% last 10m.

julia-cs: FYI customer AcmeReports DM'd: some of their streaming sessions froze and client retried -> double billing complaints starting. They flagged this to their SRE.

mike: on infra side I already see node `gpu-node-7` reporting ECC errors and intermittent thermal throttle. `nvidia-smi` output:
```:
GPU 0: TeslaX (UUID: GPU-0)
ECC errors: correctable 124, uncorrectable 2
Temp: 92C (clamped), Power: 250W
Utilization: 85% mem 70%
```

sophia: 2 uncorrectable ECC errors is bad. Could cause stalls in the runtime. Are pods on that node handling critical routes?

ashley: yes, a mix of streaming instances and some long-context gen instances pinned to that node via nodeSelector for throughput reasons.

mike: immediate mitigation plan: 1) mark node `unschedulable` and start graceful drain, 2) failover streaming traffic to fallback pool (scale up `serve-fallback`), 3) switch routing to lower-cost model variants for non-enterprise customers to preserve capacity.

ops: recommended kubectl drain command (non-destructive):
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-7
kubectl drain gpu-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60
```

sophia: ok doing cordon+drain. streaming router: moving 30% traffic to `serve-fallback` and enable fast retry with 1s backoff. doing canary now.

eng-runtime-bot: Route update: `/v1/stream` -> fallback pool applied (30%), active for 30s canary.

ashley: can we confirm no in-flight KV cache corruption when pods get migrated? we need to ensure tail tokens don't double-send.

sophia: runtime team: I triggered a cache sync flush on the migrating pods to avoid stale KV reuse: `rl-proxy flush-cache --node gpu-node-7`. Confirmed flushed.

mike: drain in progress. pods evicting, some pods reporting `OOM` during restart, but evictions are moving to other nodes. I'll watch for new p99 after full drain.

zack: p99 improving to ~1.8s after canary, p99 back under SLO for last 2m for canary traffic. global p99 still 2.4s because full rebalancing not finished.

julia-cs: updated AcmeReports: experiencing reduced errors, we routed them to fallback endpoint as a temporary measure, asking them to hold until we confirm stability. They appreciate the heads-up.

mike: cordon+drain complete. node showing hardware faults in machine logs: `mcelog` shows GPU ECC uncorrectable, thermal event spike at 1954322010.

glen-hw: from hardware side, we should schedule RMA for GPU on node `gpu-node-7`. Uncorrectable ECC + thermal suggests failing DIMMS or GPU silicon fault. Recommend replacing card and running memtest overnight.

sophia: do we want to powercycle and reprovision before RMA? Might be useful to confirm.

glen-hw: we can try a soft powercycle, but uncorrectable ECC usually indicates permanent hardware issue. I'll prepare RMA and coordinate with rack ops. ETA for swap: 3 hours on SOC ticket #HW-9921.

ashley: customer impact summary for incident channel: ~10% of streaming sessions experienced stalls/retries during window 1954321975-1954322150, p99 breached to ~4s, escalation required. No data exfiltration. Billing duplicates possible for clients with automatic retry logic.

julia-cs: I'll consolidate impacted customers and add to support tickets, offering to credit retry charges. cc @billing.

mike: follow-up ops steps: 1) keep node cordoned until RMA complete, 2) run node diagnostic on neighbor nodes to ensure not systemic, 3) add auto-drain thresholds for ECC uncorrectable >0 in future (today it wasn't set).

eng-runtime-bot: Incident note: automatic fallback activated at 1954322007. Canary success after 60s. Full rollback not required.

sophia: handoff: I'm going offline at 1954322200. @mike, please take ownership for hardware coordination and closure. I'll draft initial incident timeline and postmortem skeleton.

mike: taking over. I'll monitor for 2h and drive RMA. ping me for anything urgent. :thumbsup: \n
ashley: action items assigned:
- sophia: draft postmortem + timeline (due EOD)
- mike: RMA and confirm node reprovision (ETA 3h)
- glen-hw: coordinate hardware swap and memtest
- julia-cs: customer comms and billing review
- zack: add alert rule change to trigger immediate cordon on uncorrectable ECC >0

sophia: thanks all. quick note for postmortem: track root cause hypotheses (GPU hardware failure vs thermal runaway vs kernel panic), mitigation effectiveness, and customer impact window.

incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-1954321987 (latency spike due to GPU node degradation). Assigned: mike, sophia. Severity: Sev2.

mike: logging a short status for ops-daily: node cordoned and drained, fallback routing active, RMA initiated. Will update when swap complete.

zack: adding to runbook: add `nvidia-smi --query-ecc` periodic check and alert on uncorrectable ECC > 0.

ashley: agreed. also add a test in staging to simulate ECC/unavailable GPU to validate graceful fallback for streaming.

julia-cs: AcmeReports confirmed decreased errors after we shifted routes, still watching.

mike: last note before I start hardware coordination: no pod data loss observed, KV cache flushed before eviction, streaming resumes normally for rerouted traffic. Marking last_message at 1954322360 for this thread.

sophia: thanks team, will update with postmortem link once draft is ready. :white_check_mark:
